submissions.findingTextShort: A three-month randomized Zembrin trial provides bounded healthy-adult tolerability evidence but assessed no efficacy variables.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled single-center study enrolled 37 healthy adults and assigned standardized 2:1 Sceletium tortuosum extract (Zembrin) at 8 mg/day, 25 mg/day, or placebo for three months. Both extract doses were reported as well tolerated across vital signs, ECG, laboratory testing, physical examination, and adverse-event monitoring, but the protocol assessed no efficacy variables, so unsolicited diary comments about stress or sleep cannot be treated as treatment-effect evidence.
submissions.populationContext: Thirty-seven healthy adults; 12 received 8 mg/day Zembrin, 12 received 25 mg/day, and 13 received placebo for three months.
submissions.usageContext: Standardized proprietary 2:1 Sceletium tortuosum extract (Zembrin); preparation-specific tolerability evidence only.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Small single-center healthy-volunteer study. It supports only short-term preparation-specific tolerability and cannot establish efficacy, long-term safety, interaction safety, or safety of other Kanna preparations. The source must complete registry and semantic-attestation governance before promotion.

submissions.findingTextShort: A small crossover study found selected executive-function signals with 25 mg/day Zembrin in cognitively healthy adults.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled crossover proof-of-concept study in 21 cognitively healthy adults used 25 mg/day of proprietary Sceletium tortuosum extract (Zembrin) for three weeks and reported significant improvements in selected measures of cognitive set flexibility and executive function versus placebo, with additional exploratory mood and sleep changes.
submissions.populationContext: Twenty-one cognitively healthy adults, mean age approximately 55 years, in a short crossover proof-of-concept study.
submissions.usageContext: Proprietary standardized Zembrin extract, 25 mg once daily for three weeks; findings must not be transferred to generic Kanna products or to treatment of cognitive impairment or dementia.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Very small proof-of-concept sample with selected endpoints and proprietary-product involvement. This is preliminary human cognition evidence, not evidence that Kanna prevents or treats Alzheimer disease or other cognitive disorders. The source must complete registry and semantic-attestation governance before promotion.

submissions.findingTextShort: A single-dose Zembrin laboratory study produced mixed anxiety results: one experiment was null while another showed selected signals.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Two placebo-controlled double-blind laboratory experiments in 20 young healthy volunteers tested a single 25 mg dose of Zembrin during experimentally induced stress. The first experiment found no treatment effect on the measured mood response, while the second found lower subjective anxiety at a pre-stress time point and a treatment-by-time interaction for heart rate. The mixed pattern is tentative laboratory evidence rather than proof of clinical anxiolytic efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: Twenty young healthy volunteers exposed to short laboratory stress paradigms, not patients diagnosed with an anxiety disorder.
submissions.usageContext: Single 25 mg dose of proprietary standardized Zembrin extract; experimental stress response only.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Tiny healthy-volunteer experiments, selected time-point/physiologic findings, and a null first experiment materially limit inference. Do not generalize to sustained use, generic Kanna, or clinical treatment of anxiety. The source must complete registry and semantic-attestation governance before promotion.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2023 meta-analysis of four randomized studies found no significant anxiety difference between Sceletium tortuosum and control.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A 2023 systematic review and meta-analysis pooled four randomized studies totaling 117 adults and found no significant difference in anxiety outcomes between Sceletium tortuosum and control (RR 1.01, 95% CI 0.56 to 1.83, p=0.98; I²=0%). The small evidence base and wide confidence interval leave uncertainty, but the synthesis does not establish Kanna as an effective anxiety treatment.
submissions.populationContext: Four randomized adult studies totaling 117 participants; included studies varied in design and duration and largely used standardized extract preparations.
submissions.usageContext: Anxiety outcome synthesis; should constrain broad Kanna/Zembrin anxiolytic claims rather than erase narrower laboratory signals.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Only four small randomized studies were available, producing a wide confidence interval despite low statistical heterogeneity. The null synthesis should be retained alongside individual positive signals and should not be reframed as proof of no possible effect. The source must complete registry and semantic-attestation governance before promotion.
